subject: Clarifying SLA impact from CDN failover + partial cache degradation
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@acmehealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 16:10:23 +0000
Subject: High tail latency / 200 errors during 2026-10-28 02:13-02:42 UTC window

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

We observed elevated 95th/99th p95/p99 latencies and intermittent 5xxs for Redwood-powered inference between 02:13 and 02:42 UTC on 2026-10-28. Our instrumentation shows request timeouts and increased retries on a subset of edge POPs in us-east-1. We raised an internal alert and routed to the FastEdge CDN provider for the first-level triage — they reported a provider-side failover, but some of the request traces show KV cache misses and a burst of upstream connections that started ~02:20 UTC and continued for ~12m.

We need clarity on the root cause and whether this counts as a Redwood SLA event (service availability) or a third-party maintenance exclusion. From our side this degraded user-facing latency and increased cost. Please advise next steps and whether a credit/uptime adjustment will be available.

Attached: acme-alert-1028.txt (snippet of their alerting timeline)

Thanks,
Asha Kapoor
Senior SRE, Acme Health

From: cdn-support@fastedge.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 01:14:20 +0000
Subject: Re: Inquiry: FastEdge failover 2026-10-28 — maintenance window details

Hi all,

EdgeCore / FastEdge NOC here. We performed an emergency region failover in us-east-1 starting 2026-10-28T02:10:50Z due to a control-plane replication stall. The automated failover completed at 2026-10-28T02:25:10Z. We observed transient TCP connection resets at ~02:17Z as sessions drained; these manifested as higher retry counts for upstream origins.

Attached: fastedge-maint-1028.pdf (failover timeline and NOC notes).

Notes:
- This was an operational failover initiated by our control plane, not a scheduled maintenance.
- Our probes show the main failover activity finished by 02:25Z; however, downstream cache warm-up and origin reconnection patterns varied by POP — some POPs show increased cache misses and origin requests until ~02:38Z.

We consider the interval 02:10:50Z-02:25:10Z our failover window. Anything after that is dependent on customer edge warming and origin behavior and isn't part of our maintenance/windowed exclusion by default. Happy to work with Redwood and Acme to reconcile probe evidence.

Regards,
EdgeCore NOC
noc@edgecore.io
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com, cdn-support@fastedge.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:34:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency / 200 errors during 2026-10-28 02:13-02:42 UTC window — probe evidence

Folks — I pulled our end-to-end traces and server logs. Summary:

- Redwood probes (global active probes) show a first anomaly at 02:12:11Z with a small number of 504s from a subset of edge gateways.
- At 02:16:40Z we see a spike in KV cache evictions on gateway cluster gw-us-east-3; eviction rate jumps 6x and correlates with increased origin fetches.
- Our backend telemetry indicates that although FastEdge failover (per their timeline) finished by 02:25:10Z, the bulk of elevated origin traffic and cache cold starts continued until 02:36Z across ~3 POPs.
- The impact on error budget: if you count the entire 02:10:50Z-02:36:00Z window as an outage, the visible customer-facing error rate exceeds the p99 SLO threshold for a sustained 9m period within that window.

Analysis and ask:
- Per our standard SLA, third-party control plane failovers where the vendor identifies a hard failover window are treated as potential exclusions only for their explicit failover period. Any continuing degradation caused by downstream cache warming / origin load is normally considered part of the customer's service window unless the vendor accepts responsibility.
- Given that our probes demonstrate KV cache invalidations on Redwood gateways concurrent with the failover and extending past FastEdge's declared window, we believe a split attribution is reasonable. Specifically, propose apportioning the total impacted time as: vendor-controlled failover window (02:10:50Z-02:25:10Z) = FastEdge responsibility; residual cold-start and eviction-driven degradation (02:25:11Z-02:36:00Z) = mixed responsibility, with Redwood accepting responsibility for 40% of that residual window (cache warming) and FastEdge accepting 60% (delayed session handover).

Attached: probe-samples-1028.csv (selected traces), slo-apportionment-worksheet.xlsx (worked example).

I recommend we present this apportionment to Acme and FastEdge and request a formal credit for the portion attributable to FastEdge's control-plane failover.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: ops@acmehealth.com, cdn-support@fastedge.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency / 200 errors during 2026-10-28 02:13-02:42 UTC window — proposed apportionment

Thanks everyone — helpful thread and thanks EdgeCore for the timeline.

Proposed next steps (I will coordinate):
1) FastEdge: please confirm acceptance/feedback on the vendor portion (02:10:50Z-02:25:10Z) being your responsibility for crediting purposes. If you accept, confirm the credit calculation method (we prefer a token/time-weighted apportionment consistent with Redwood billing signals).
2) Redwood (Marissa/Karthik): we'll finalize the residual apportionment worksheet and publish the worked calculation to the support ticket.
3) Acme: once both parties agree to apportionment percentages, Redwood will issue a consolidated credit for the portion allocated to FastEdge (we will pass through the vendor credit where applicable and adjust the customer's uptime ledger).

If we don't get vendor agreement by EOD Thu 2026-11-05 we'll escalate to account-level review and consider applying a conservative credit to Acme pending vendor confirmation.
